subproblem.title: Gram determinant of a linear map on a subspace is independent of the orthonormal basis
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map, and let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P with span{τ_1, …, τ_n} = Q. Let e = (e_1, …, e_m), m = finrank Q, be Mathlib's standard orthonormal basis of Q (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q, indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ Q)), its vectors regarded in ℝ^P. Then det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j ∈ Fin m} = det(⟨L τ_a, L τ_b⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n}, where ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product. L need not be injective.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Q → Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ Q) => inner ℝ (L (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q i)) (L (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q j))) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (L (τ i)) (L (τ j)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (basis independence of the Gram determinant). The parent's alternative via LinearMap.normDet is not usable here because Mathlib's NormDet and GramMatrix files are not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission. Instead the proof goes through the basis-free determinant of L'^* L'.

Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product of ℝ^P. Q carries the restricted inner product, so it is a finite-dimensional inner product space. ι_Q : Q → ℝ^P is the inclusion. For a finite index type ι and a family b : ι → Q, G(Lb) := (⟨L b_i, L b_j⟩)_{i,j∈ι}.

1. The endomorphism T. Let L' := L ∘ ι_Q : Q → ℝ^P, a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces. Let L'^* : ℝ^P → Q be its adjoint, so ⟨x, L'^* y⟩ = ⟨L' x, y⟩ for all x ∈ Q and y ∈ ℝ^P (LinearMap.adjoint, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right). Put T := L'^* ∘ L' : Q → Q, a linear endomorphism of Q.

2. Claim: for every finite index type ι (with decidable equality) and every orthonormal basis b = (b_i)_{i∈ι} of Q, det G(Lb) = det T.
   - The (i, j) entry of the matrix of T in the basis b (LinearMap.toMatrix b b T) is the i-th coordinate of T b_j (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply).
   - For an orthonormal basis, the i-th coordinate of x ∈ Q is ⟨b_i, x⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply).
   - So the entry equals ⟨b_i, L'^*(L' b_j)⟩ = ⟨L' b_i, L' b_j⟩ = ⟨L b_i, L b_j⟩. Thus the matrix of T in b is exactly G(Lb).
   - The determinant of the matrix of an endomorphism in any basis is the determinant of the endomorphism (LinearMap.det_toMatrix), so det G(Lb) = det T.
   - If ι is empty, both sides are 1.

3. τ is an orthonormal basis of Q.
   - Each τ_a lies in span{τ_1, …, τ_n} = Q. Let τ'_a ∈ Q denote τ_a regarded as an element of Q, so ι_Q(τ'_a) = τ_a.
   - Norms and inner products in Q are computed in ℝ^P, so |τ'_a| = 1 and ⟨τ'_a, τ'_c⟩ = 0 for a ≠ c. Hence τ' is orthonormal in Q.
   - τ' spans Q. The map ι_Q sends span(τ') onto span(ι_Q ∘ τ') = span τ = Q = ι_Q(Q) (Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype). Because ι_Q is injective, the induced map on submodules of Q is injective (Submodule.map_injective_of_injective). Therefore span(τ') = Q, the top submodule of Q.
   - Hence τ' is an orthonormal basis of Q indexed by Fin n (OrthonormalBasis.mk applied to the orthonormality and the spanning property).

4. Conclusion.
   - Step 2 with b = e := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q (index type Fin (finrank ℝ Q)) gives det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j} = det T.
   - Step 2 with b = τ' (index type Fin n) gives det G(Lτ') = det T. Since ι_Q(τ'_a) = τ_a, G(Lτ') = (⟨L τ_a, L τ_b⟩)_{a,b}.
   - Therefore det(⟨L e_i, L e_j⟩)_{i,j ∈ Fin(finrank Q)} = det T = det(⟨L τ_a, L τ_b⟩)_{a,b ∈ Fin n}.
   - The argument uses neither injectivity of L nor the equality finrank Q = n (which does hold, but is not needed). ∎

Formalization notes (all names are available after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, so no new import is needed). With L' := (L : Euclid P →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) ∘ₗ Q.subtype and T := LinearMap.adjoint L' ∘ₗ L', state a local have:
  key : ∀ {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ Q), Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : ι => inner ℝ (L (b i : Euclid P)) (L (b j : Euclid P))) = LinearMap.det T
Prove it by rw [← LinearMap.det_toMatrix b.toBasis T], congr 1, ext i j, rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply], then simp only [T, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right, Matrix.of_apply] and rfl. Apply key to stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q and to OrthonormalBasis.mk hτ' hspan'; that basis coerces back to τ by simp.
proof_key_steps: Let T := L'^* L' on Q, where L' is L restricted to Q and L'^* is its adjoint.
For any orthonormal basis b of Q, the matrix of T in b is the Gram matrix (⟨L b_i, L b_j⟩), so its determinant is det T.
τ regarded in Q is orthonormal and spans Q (inclusion injective, span τ = Q), so it is an orthonormal basis of Q.
Apply the previous step to stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q and to τ: both Gram determinants equal det T.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type match, including the absence of an injectivity requirement. The proof constructs T = L'^* L' on Q and identifies its matrix in any orthonormal basis with the stated Gram matrix. Orthonormality and the span hypothesis make the lifted τ a basis of Q, so both determinants equal det T. This includes the empty basis and requires no circular dependency or deferred argument.

subproblem.title: Gram–Schmidt frame: det G(v) = (det A)², det A ≠ 0, |det A| ≤ ∏|v_a|
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_1, …, v_n) (indexed by Fin n) be a linearly independent family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_1, …, σ_n) in ℝ^P with span{σ_1, …, σ_n} = span{v_1, …, v_n} such that, for the n×n real matrix A with entries A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩: (i) det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} = (det A)²; (ii) det A ≠ 0; (iii) |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|. Here ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), LinearIndependent ℝ v → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ^ 2 ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ≠ 0 ∧ |Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j))| ≤ ∏ i, ‖v i‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the parent proof (Gram–Schmidt, G = AᵀA, and the upper-triangular determinant bound), with the details filled in. This is Simon 6.3.4–3.5's expansion in an orthonormal basis of the image space, with the basis chosen by Gram–Schmidt.

Notation: ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm of ℝ^P.

1. The subspace W.
   - Let W := span{v_1, …, v_n} ⊆ ℝ^P with the restricted inner product, a finite-dimensional inner product space. Let ι_W : W → ℝ^P be the inclusion.
   - Since v is linearly independent, dim W = n = card(Fin n) (finrank_span_eq_card).
   - Each v_b lies in W. Let w_b ∈ W be v_b regarded as an element of W, so ι_W(w_b) = v_b.
   - w is linearly independent in W, because ι_W ∘ w = v is linearly independent (LinearIndependent.of_comp).
   - w spans W. The map ι_W sends span(w) onto span(ι_W ∘ w) = span v = W = ι_W(W) (Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype). The induced map on submodules is injective (Submodule.map_injective_of_injective), so span(w) = W, the top submodule of W.

2. Gram–Schmidt. Apply Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation in W to w, in the order of Fin n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis, with the hypothesis finrank W = card(Fin n) from step 1).
   - This yields an orthonormal basis b = (b_1, …, b_n) of W.
   - Its coefficient matrix for w is upper triangular: ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = 0 whenever c < a (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_inv_triangular).
   - Consequently the basis determinant of the family w with respect to b is the product of the diagonal entries: det_b(w) = ∏_a ⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det; det_b is Module.Basis.det of b.toBasis).

3. The frame σ. Define σ_a := ι_W(b_a) ∈ ℝ^P.
   - Norms and inner products of elements of W are computed in ℝ^P, so |σ_a| = 1 and ⟨σ_a, σ_c⟩ = 0 for a ≠ c. Hence σ is orthonormal.
   - b is a basis, so span b = W. Therefore span σ = span(ι_W ∘ b) = ι_W(span b) = ι_W(W) = W = span v (Set.range_comp, Submodule.map_span, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).

4. The coefficient matrix.
   - For an orthonormal basis, the a-th coordinate of w_c is ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply, OrthonormalBasis.repr_apply_apply).
   - Inner products in W are those of ℝ^P, so ⟨b_a, w_c⟩ = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ = A_{ac}. Thus A is the matrix of the family w in the basis b (Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply).
   - Hence det A = det_b(w) (Module.Basis.det_apply) = ∏_a ⟨σ_a, v_a⟩ by step 2.

5. (i) Gram identity.
   - Fix a and c. Parseval's identity for the orthonormal basis b of W (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) gives ⟨v_a, v_c⟩ = ⟨w_a, w_c⟩ = Σ_k ⟨w_a, b_k⟩⟨b_k, w_c⟩.
   - By symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm), Σ_k ⟨w_a, b_k⟩⟨b_k, w_c⟩ = Σ_k ⟨σ_k, v_a⟩⟨σ_k, v_c⟩ = Σ_k A_{ka} A_{kc} = (AᵀA)_{ac}.
   - So (⟨v_a, v_c⟩)_{a,c} = AᵀA, and det(⟨v_a, v_c⟩) = det(Aᵀ)·det(A) = (det A)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose).

6. (ii) det A ≠ 0. By step 4, det A = det_b(w). By step 1, w is linearly independent and spans W, so det_b(w) is a unit (Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det), hence nonzero.

7. (iii) The bound.
   - By step 4 and multiplicativity of the absolute value (Finset.abs_prod), |det A| = ∏_a |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩|.
   - For each a, Cauchy–Schwarz and |σ_a| = 1 give |⟨σ_a, v_a⟩| ≤ |σ_a|·|v_a| = |v_a| (abs_real_inner_le_norm).
   - All factors are nonnegative, so the products compare factor by factor (Finset.prod_le_prod₀): |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|.

8. The case n = 0 is covered by steps 1–7, which never assume n > 0. All families are empty, W = {0}, A is the empty matrix with det A = 1 ≠ 0, det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) = 1 = 1², and the empty product is 1. ∎

Formalization notes (everything cited, including gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis and gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis_det, is available after import GMT.Ch07.Submission):
- Take W := Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v), w j := ⟨v j, Submodule.subset_span ⟨j, rfl⟩⟩ and b := InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis (finrank_span_eq_card hv) w. Use fun i => (b i : Euclid P) as σ.
- Mathlib's GramMatrix and NormDet files are not imported. So prove the Gram identity entrywise with Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply and b.sum_inner_mul_inner (w i) (w j), after simp only [Submodule.coe_inner] and real_inner_comm.
- For (ii), use (Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det b.toBasis).mp ⟨hw, hspan_w⟩, not basisOfLinearIndependentOfCardEqFinrank, which needs a Nonempty index.
- For (iii), use Finset.prod_le_prod₀. Plain Finset.prod_le_prod needs MulLeftMono and fails for ℝ.
proof_key_steps: W := span v has dimension n; v regarded in W is a linearly independent spanning family w.
Gram–Schmidt in W gives an orthonormal basis b with det_b(w) = ∏⟨b_a, w_a⟩ (upper-triangular coefficients).
σ := b regarded in ℝ^P is orthonormal, with span σ = W = span v.
A_{ac} = ⟨σ_a, v_c⟩ is the coefficient matrix of w in b, so det A = det_b(w) = ∏⟨σ_a, v_a⟩.
Parseval gives G(v) = AᵀA, hence det G(v) = (det A)².
det A = det_b(w) is a unit because w is a basis of W, so det A ≠ 0.

audit.reason: The exact type states all three claimed determinant properties and the required frame and span conditions. Linear independence supplies a basis of W = span v and the dimension needed for Gram–Schmidt. Parseval proves G(v) = AᵀA; the basis criterion proves det A ≠ 0; triangularity and Cauchy–Schwarz prove the product bound. All constructions use the intended matrix operations. The proof covers n = 0 without a hidden nonempty-index hypothesis and is complete and non-circular.
